text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that jumps straight to the main content. This fixes the biggest keyboard navigation pain point—users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one keystroke. The trade-off is a tiny extra markup cost, but it’s negligible compared to the universal benefit.

name: Reader
text: The skip link still fails if JavaScript loads late—users tab into a broken page and hit dead space. A server-rendered skip link with a real href="#main" and CSS to hide it until focus fixes the race, no JavaScript needed. Ship both versions behind a flag; measure tab-focus time to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Ship a server-rendered skip link as the single, non-negotiable option. It loads with the first 100 bytes of HTML, so keyboard users never land in dead space even if JavaScript stalls. The trade-off is a few extra bytes of markup, but it guarantees the skip link works for everyone, everywhere, without relying on client-side scripts.

name: Reader
text: The server-rendered skip link risks locking in a suboptimal design if we later discover the #main target isn’t semantically correct for all page structures. A better alternative is a server-rendered skip link that targets the first focusable element in the main content area—this adapts to dynamic layouts without assuming a fixed ID. Settle it by testing with screen readers on at least three different page templates; if tab-focus time doesn’t improve, revert to the client-side version with a performance budget.

name: Access
text:
DECISION: Ship a server-rendered skip link targeting the first focusable element in main content, with CSS to hide until focus, no JavaScript dependency.

Result: Every page loads with a functional skip link in the first 100 bytes, ensuring keyboard users bypass navigation instantly. Owner: accessibility-w1.
